hypotheses.justification: The only place the proof uses `[NeZero P]` is to build `NeZero (P * M₁)` (line 362) so that `ModularCurve.surjective_specialLinearGroup_map_zmod (P * M₁)` applies. The theorem is still true when `P = 0`: then `hcop : Nat.Coprime 0 M₁` together with `Nat.coprime_zero_left (M₁) : Nat.Coprime 0 M₁ ↔ M₁ = 1` (Init/Data/Nat/Coprime.lean) forces `M₁ = 1`. Taking `g₁ = g`, the first conjunct `mapN 0 g = mapN 0 g` is `rfl` (no property of `ZMod 0` is needed), and the second is `mapN 1 g = 1`, which holds because `ZMod 1` is a subsingleton (`ZMod.subsingleton_iff`), hence so is `Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) (ZMod 1)` (`Matrix.subsingleton`) and its subtype `SL(2, ZMod 1)`. So: `by_cases hP : P = 0`; in the zero case substitute `M₁ = 1` and use `g₁ = g` (the second goal closes by `Subsingleton.elim`), otherwise `haveI : NeZero P := ⟨hP⟩` and run the existing argument verbatim (now `P * M₁ ≠ 0` since `NeZero M₁` is still assumed, so line 362 still works). Since this is a separate case split from the one for `[NeZero M₁]`, the two can also be deleted together.

Here too the instance is used in the proof only to obtain `NeZero (P * M₁)`. If `M₁ = 0`, then `hcop : Nat.Coprime P 0` and `Nat.coprime_zero_right (P) : Nat.Coprime P 0 ↔ P = 1` (Init/Data/Nat/Coprime.lean) force `P = 1`. Take `g₁ = 1`: `mapN 1 1 = mapN 1 g` because `ZMod 1` is a subsingleton (`ZMod.subsingleton_iff`), so `SL(2, ZMod 1)` is a subsingleton via `Matrix.subsingleton`, and the second conjunct `mapN 0 1 = 1` is `map_one`. In the remaining case `M₁ ≠ 0` one sets `haveI : NeZero M₁ := ⟨hM⟩` and reuses the existing proof unchanged (`P ≠ 0` still comes from the retained `[NeZero P]`, so `P * M₁ ≠ 0` and `surjective_specialLinearGroup_map_zmod (P * M₁)` applies). Note `hcop` does not by itself imply `M₁ ≠ 0` (e.g. `P = 1, M₁ = 0`), which is why the degenerate case has to be treated explicitly; it is still provable, so the hypothesis is deletable. This deletion is compatible with deleting `[NeZero P]` as well.
